transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t seem to get things in order anymore. My kitchen table is just covered with papers—my husband’s appointment things, church flyers, notes from the senior center, lists I started and didn’t finish. I sit down to sort it, and I just… don’t know what to do first. Then somehow the whole day is gone.
Have you noticed yourself forgetting recent conversations or events, like something someone told you yesterday?

Yes… not always conversations exactly, but I do forget things people asked me to do. I’ve missed returning calls, and I’ve left bills buried under mail. My daughter will ask me to run an errand and then later I realize I never did it. And with my husband’s appointments… more than once I forgot to confirm them until it was too late.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or noticed that you've lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
I don’t think so… not in a clear way. I get frustrated, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been especially sad, and I still like the things I usually like when I actually get to them.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, more than seems necessary, about things like your husband's health, finances, or other everyday matters—and do you have trouble controlling that worry?
I… I wouldn’t say I worry all the time, no. I mean, there are things on my mind, of course, but I don’t think it’s worry exactly. It’s more… trying to keep up with everything.
Over the past year or so, would you say these memory and organizing problems have been gradually getting worse, or have they stayed about the same?

It’s been… about the same level of trouble for maybe a year and a few months. Around when my husband started needing regular help with appointments and day-to-day arrangements, that’s when it really became noticeable.

Do you notice these same problems with memory and staying organized in other parts of your life—like when you're doing things unrelated to your husband's care, such as hobbies, shopping, or managing your own affairs?

Yes… it’s not just his care, I guess. I came in because I just can’t seem to get things in order anymore. My kitchen table is covered with papers—his appointment things, church flyers, senior-center notes, lists I start and don’t finish—and I’ll sit there looking at it, not knowing what to do first. Then somehow the day is gone.

Have you been diagnosed with or treated for any medical conditions—like a stroke, diabetes, thyroid problems, or head injury—or started any new medications around the time these organizing and memory difficulties began?
I don’t think so… not that I can recall. I haven’t had anything like that come up around then. I’d have to check, maybe, but nothing stands out to me.

When you think about everything that's piled up—especially since your husband started needing more help—do you feel overwhelmed, anxious, or stressed by that situation itself, separate from just having trouble organizing things?
I don’t know… I suppose it’s stressful to look at all of it, yes. But I’m not sure if it’s separate from the organizing part. It all kind of feels like the same mess to me.
Have your husband, daughter, or anyone else noticed you repeating the same questions or stories, or seeming confused about the day, date, or where you are?

I’m not sure. I don’t think anyone’s said I’m confused about where I am or anything like that. My daughter may get impatient if I ask something again, but… I don’t know that she’s called it repeating stories.

Are there times—like when a family member helps with your husband's care or things settle down for a few days—when you notice your ability to keep track of things and stay organized gets noticeably better?

Maybe a little, but… not really enough that I’d say it clears up. I still end up at the kitchen table with all these papers—my husband’s appointments, church things, senior-center notes, lists I started and didn’t finish—and I just sit there trying to figure out what comes first. Then somehow the day’s gone.
Have you noticed yourself having trouble finding the right words, or forgetting the names of common objects or people you know well?
Not really… I mean, I might pause sometimes, like anyone, but I haven’t noticed forgetting names of things or people I know well.

If someone else took over your husband's appointments and errands for a while and that stress went away, do you think your memory and trouble organizing things would go back to normal, or do you think it would still be a problem?

I think it would still be a problem. Maybe less pressure, but… I came in because I can’t get things in order anymore. The table gets covered with his appointment papers and church flyers and notes, and I just sit there trying to decide what comes first. Then the day’s gone.

Have you noticed any changes in your ability to handle tasks that used to come easily to you—like managing your finances, following a recipe you know well, or figuring out how to use something familiar, like your phone or the stove?

Yes… I suppose so. I had to step back from leading a big event at the senior center, which was… embarrassing. And my daughter’s been checking over bills and appointments now, just to make sure I haven’t missed something. She doesn’t really trust me to keep it all straight by myself anymore.

I guess the main thing is… I’ve had to step back from things. I gave up leading a big event at the senior center, and now my daughter checks the bills and appointments after me. She just doesn’t trust that I’ll keep it all straight on my own anymore.

I know I already said it, but… yes. I had to let go of leading that senior-center event. And my daughter’s been looking over the bills and appointments after I do them. She doesn’t really trust me to keep it all straight by myself now.
Aside from your husband's care, have you noticed trouble managing your own things—like keeping track of your own medications, paying your personal bills, or balancing your own checkbook?

Yes… some. I’ve missed returning calls, and I’ll find bills still sitting under a stack of mail. I’ve forgotten errands I told my daughter I’d do. And with my husband’s appointments, more than once I realized too late I never called to confirm.

When your daughter or husband remind you about something that happened earlier that day, are you able to recall it once they mention it, or does it still seem unfamiliar to you even after being reminded?
I’m not really sure. Most of the time, if they remind me, I can sort of place it… but I don’t know that I’ve paid close attention to whether it feels unfamiliar or not.
Have you ever gotten confused or lost your way while driving or walking somewhere familiar, like your own neighborhood or a store you go to often?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t gotten lost in my neighborhood or anything like that. Not that I’ve noticed.
When someone teaches you something new—like a new phone feature or a new routine—do you find you still can't remember it even after being shown or told several times?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed that exactly… sometimes I need things shown again, but I couldn’t say if it’s after several times or not.

Can you think of a specific time recently—completely unrelated to your husband's care or errands, like reading a book, following a TV show plot, or playing a game—when you noticed the same kind of trouble concentrating or keeping track of things?

Yes… I guess at the senior center, if I’m trying to write something down or plan out what I’m doing, and a couple people start talking nearby, I kind of follow their conversation instead. Or if the TV is on in the next room, same thing. Then I look back and I’ve lost my place.
